messages:
irina: Nightly eval alert: llamaX_v2-q4f (13B quant) failing 38% of the commonsense prompt set vs 3% baseline after yesterday's fused-attn reorder PR #4721 :warning: @sam @matt

jess (eval-bot): CI link: https://ci.redwood/internal/nightly/1718765400 - failing bucket = commonsense_prompts, examples attached in the job artifacts

sam: Ack. Pulling the job now. Do we know which commit exactly? Could be RNG/state or kv-cache ordering.

matt: That was my deploy - commit ab12f9e83. Improved throughput ~+12% on 13B. I ran unit/regression but not full nightly across prompt buckets.

irina: Regression unit tests passed, but the nightly coverage found these generative regressions. Two patterns: (1) early truncation for long context prompts, (2) small but consistent token-shift + weird repetition in prose answers. Examples below.

irina: ```
PROMPT: "Explain why a comet's tail points away from the sun."
EXPECTED: "The tail points away because solar wind and radiation pressure push dust and gas outward from the comet's nucleus."
ACTUAL: "The tail points away because the comet and the sun. The tail points away..."  <-- truncated/repeated, loses causal clause after token 28

PROMPT: "Solve: If a train leaves at 5pm..."
EXPECTED: "The time difference is 2 hours..."
ACTUAL: "The time difference is" <no continuing tokens>  <-- early stop
```

sam: Interesting. Could be an off-by-one in KV write index or a sampling state reset. Can you paste the reproduce command?

irina: Repro (from eval machine):
```bash
curl -X POST https://hosted.redwood/api/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY' -d '{"model":"llamaX_v2-q4f","prompt":"Explain why a comet's tail points away from the sun.","max_tokens":128,"seed":42}'
```

ci-bot: Started job 9853 reproducer on ab12f9e83 (runner: gpu-canary-3). Will post logs when done.

jess: Also seeing that with deterministic seeds the outputs diverge from baseline at step 3 in many cases. That usually points at a non-deterministic buffer write or a kernel that depends on uninitialized memory.

matt: Rolling back fused-attn reorder on canary hosts (gpu-canary-{1,3}) to previous kernel ct01 for now. Will monitor regressions.

sam: I'll run a quick script to compare sampler_state and kv lengths across steps. Pushing script to /evals/tmp/attn_drift_check.sh and kicking off 100 seeds.

irina: Please also verify behavior with seq_len > 1024 and with prefix caching on. The early stop seems correlated with longer contexts.

matt: Agreed. If quick mitigation needed: enable fallback to unfused-attn path for quantized models in routing rules until we root cause.

sam: Issue opened: https://issues.redwood/5789 - contains reproducer, job artifacts and short diff of fused-attn change. Assigned to @sam and @matt.

ci-bot: Job 9853 completed. Key log lines:
```
[2024-06-18 02:14:12] sampler_state[step=0] = 0x3f8a2c...
[2024-06-18 02:14:12] sampler_state[step=1] = 0x1d4b0f...
[2024-06-18 02:14:13] sampler_state[step=3] = 0x7f00ff...  <-- divergence from baseline at step 3
[2024-06-18 02:14:13] kv_cache_write_index=1025 (expected <=1024)  <-- suspicious
```

jess: I'll run the nightly eval again across all buckets to see scope (math, code, chit-chat). Will post update in ~30m.

sam: Tagging @eng-runtime for visibility and asking for a quick kernel-forensics pass.

irina: Thanks all. Keep notes here. If we confirm kv index overflow, that explains token shifts and early stops.

matt: On it. I'll add assert/guard in the kernel to prevent writes > seq_len and re-run microbench.

irina: Good plan. If we need to, flip routing fallback for q4f models in the next 15m to stop customer regressions.

sam: Will coordinate rollout/rollback with platform.

irina: Update: jess reports scope = commonsense + prose primarily, not math-heavy prompts (so far).

ci-bot: Nightly re-run scheduled. Will update when done. :gear:
